title: Macbeth Key Quotes Stretch
welcome_lead: Stretch: turn quotes into arguments. How do these six lines map the play's moral collapse?
meta_desc: GCSE English Literature — using key Macbeth quotes to build essay arguments.
final_note: You sequenced six quotes into a moral arc and practised the quote-led essay technique.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Blood appears in every act.

Act 1: Macbeth is 'bath'd in reeking wounds' (heroic). Act 2: 'Neptune's ocean' won't wash it (guilt). Act 5: 'out, damned spot' (madness). One motif tracks the moral journey.

Use the PEEL formula: Point, Evidence, Explanation, Link.

POINT: Macbeth willingly chooses evil. EVIDENCE: 'Stars, hide your fires.' EXPLANATION: the imperative shows he commands the cosmos to hide his sin. LINK: this prepares us for his later regicide.

Place the six quotes in moral order:

1) 'Fair is foul' (chaos), 2) 'Stars, hide your fires' (temptation), 3) 'serpent under't' (deception), 4) 'Is this a dagger' (action), 5) 'Out, damned spot' (guilt), 6) 'Tomorrow' (despair). That's your essay skeleton.

options: Dystopian fiction predicts what will actually happen in 100 years.
Themes are just symbols repeated through the book.
A theme is an abstract idea or concern the text explores (e.g. mortality); a symbol is a concrete image that stands for something else (e.g. a skull).
A theme is the title of the book.

The claim that judging a text by what the author 'intended' is fallacious — the text's meaning lies in the work itself, not the author's stated or guessed intentions.
